question: What is the primary goal of emergency nursing when managing a life-threatening condition?

options.B: Completing a full health history before acting
options.C: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible

explanation: Emergency nursing focuses on acting fast to save lives when a patient's condition can quickly deteriorate. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is time considered so critical when dealing with emergency medical conditions?

options.A: Hospital regulations require fast bed turnover
options.B: Insurance companies will not pay for slow care
options.C: Doctors refuse to see patients who wait too long
options.D: Delays can lead to rapid deterioration and death

explanation: In critical emergencies, minutes matter because a failing body system quickly causes permanent harm or death if not supported. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h1)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the ABCDE emergency assessment framework?
explanation: The ABCDE acronym stands for Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, and Exposure. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h2)

question: A patient arrives in the emergency unit after a severe motorcycle crash. According to the ABCDE rule, what should the nurse check first?
explanation: Airway is always the top priority in the ABCDE approach because an obstructed airway causes death faster than anything else. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which sign is a clinical indicator of severe respiratory distress in an adult patient?

options.A: Relaxed posture in a flat bed

explanation: When breathing becomes very hard, patients use their neck and chest muscles to help force air in and out. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is a silent chest in a patient with severe asthma considered a dangerous emergency?

options.A: It means air is no longer moving in or out of the lungs
options.B: It is a normal finding during deep sleep
options.C: It shows that the inhaler medication worked successfully
options.D: It indicates the asthma attack has completely resolved

explanation: A silent chest means the airways are so tight or blocked that air cannot move at all, which signals immediate respiratory arrest. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is a primary clinical feature of hemodynamic instability?

options.A: High fever with shivering and chills
options.B: Elevated urine output above normal limits
options.C: Gradual weight gain over several weeks
options.D: Inadequate blood flow to vital organs

explanation: Hemodynamic instability simply means the circulation is failing to supply enough blood to keep organs working properly. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why can a normal blood pressure reading sometimes be misleading in early cardiovascular shock?

options.A: Only the pulse rate matters during a cardiac crisis
options.B: Heart conditions never affect blood pressure numbers
options.C: The body's compensation keeps pressure normal before it crashes
options.D: Blood pressure cuffs are notoriously inaccurate in emergency rooms

explanation: The body works hard to keep blood pressure stable by narrowing blood vessels, meaning the patient can suddenly crash later. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the underlying physiological problem in all types of shock?

options.B: Inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular hypoxia
options.C: An excess of oxygen in the circulating blood
options.D: A sudden increase in overall body temperature

explanation: Shock occurs when cells do not receive enough oxygen-rich blood to perform normal metabolism. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h5)

question: A patient with severe internal bleeding from a car crash is most likely to develop which type of shock?
explanation: Hypovolemic shock is caused by a drastic loss of blood volume circulating in the body. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which quick bedside test should a nurse perform immediately for any patient presenting with sudden confusion?
explanation: Low blood sugar is a common, easily reversible cause of altered mental status that must be checked right away. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h6)

question: What do the letters in the FAST stroke mnemonic stand for to help recognize warning signs?

options.A: Fluid intake, Activity level, Skin turgor, Eyes check
options.B: Fast breathing, Airway blockage, Sound tone, Temperature
options.C: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call

explanation: FAST is a simple public health tool used to spot the most common stroke symptoms quickly. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which major organ system is most immediately threatened by severe hyperkalemia (high blood potassium)?
explanation: High potassium levels dangerously alter the electrical conduction of the heart, leading to fatal arrhythmias. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following conditions is a classic example of a metabolic crisis in diabetes?
explanation: Diabetic ketoacidosis is an acute, life-threatening metabolic emergency caused by severe insulin deficiency and acid buildup. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why is continuous re-evaluation necessary in emergency nursing care?

options.A: Patient conditions can change rapidly and unpredictably
options.B: Hospital policies require charting every fifteen minutes
options.C: Patients get bored if nurses do not check on them
options.D: Doctors will not review charts without new updates

explanation: Emergency patients are unstable, meaning a stable patient can deteriorate suddenly and require a shift in priorities. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h8)

question: A nurse is caring for four emergency patients. Which patient should the nurse attend to FIRST?

options.A: A patient with a minor scalp laceration needing stitches
options.B: A patient with a closed wrist fracture in mild pain
options.C: A patient with severe stridor and throat swelling
options.D: A patient complaining of a mild headache for three days

explanation: Stridor indicates an upper airway obstruction, which is an immediate life threat that takes top priority over pain or minor injuries. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h8)
